quote: Meat is cooked on shared tabletop yakiniku grills alongside items brushed with soy-sauce-based tare, creating likely cross-contact for gluten-sensitive/celiac diners; no dedicated gluten-free grill or preparation area was found in any source.
found: Official group page: 「卸）神保町食肉センターグループは排気を外に出すガス式テーブルロースターを用いています…お客様自身がお客様のお好みで焼くシーン」 and 「素材の味を最大限に生かす為、あたり（味付け）を決めさせていただいております…創業以来、改良に改良を重ねた門外支出の「秘伝のタレ」」
method: 2 (uncited claim) — found the operator's own page; corroborated by hotpepper snippet 「門外不出のこだわりのタレ！…「秘伝のタレ」で味付けをしております」 via Yahoo Japan
note: UNCITED but TRUE and repairable. The operator itself states every table has a shared gas roaster the diner cooks on and that ALL meat arrives pre-seasoned with a house tare chosen by the shop. Cite http://www.jinbo.tokyo/strong_point/ .

quote: The restaurant's tare-marinated cuts follow standard yakiniku practice using soy sauce, which in Japan is typically wheat-based unless specified otherwise; no wheat-free soy sauce or tamari alternative was mentioned in any source.
found: 「創業以来、改良に改良を重ねた門外支出の「秘伝のタレ」」 (jinbo.tokyo/strong_point/); Tabelog 備考 and お店のPR carry no allergen or tamari statement of any kind; the whole official site has no allergen page.
note: UNCITED but the absence half is verified. Sharpen the wording: the tare is not merely undocumented, the shop advertises it as 門外不出 / 秘伝 (never disclosed), so 'ask staff about the tare' cannot produce an ingredient list. That is worth saying in gf_detail.

quote: Some cuts (liver, heart, some pork/beef) are offered plain with salt (shio) rather than tare, which structurally avoids the soy-sauce marinade if requested.
found: 「店名 神保町食肉センター上野店 / 住所 東京都台東区上野4-4-3 ハトヤビル1号館 2F」 and 「4種類の肉と味が組み合わさったA・B・Cの中からまず1つを選ぶシステム…ただし、肉の味は固定であることに注意したい」 / 「つけダレも無いため、塩味だけだとやや飽きが来る」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited article + 1 plain fetch of the operator site
note: TWO DEFECTS AT ONCE. (a) SIBLING-BRANCH CITATION: the cited RocketNews piece is a visit to the UENO branch (上野4-4-3), not the Jimbocho honten this record is about. (b) The article CONTRADICTS the claim's operative words: 「肉の味は固定」 — the seasoning per cut is fixed and cannot be requested, and the operator's own site says 「あたり（味付け）を決めさせていただいております」. A celiac told they can 'request shio' would be misled. Also note the Ueno set pairs 塩 cuts with a ミソ味 cut (ネックピートロ) whose miso 「網が序盤から盛大に焦げ付く」 — the shared-grill residue is miso, not soy tare, and 麦味噌 is a barley risk the record never mentions.

quote: No explicit statement was found about the wheat content of the tare/soy sauce used, but standard Japanese yakitori tare and oden broth typically contain wheat-based soy sauce, so this should be assumed present unless staff confirm otherwise.
found: Official お料理 page: 「ご注文は、1本から承ります。塩・タレからお選びください。」 and, for the oden, 「北海道日高昆布と鶏のガラから弱火で時間をかけ丁寧に煮出したお出汁です。鶏がらを使うことでさっぱりとしたコクのあるお出汁にしあげています。」 — no soy sauce, no allergen note anywhere on the page.
method: 2 (uncited claim) — located the shop's own full menu page
note: UNCITED and WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It warns about a soy-sauce assumption the shop never makes, while missing the actual wheat: the oden pot simmers 「くるま麩」(300円) — kuruma-fu is pure wheat gluten — and 「ちくわぶ」(200円), which is wheat flour, so the shared oden dashi is wheat-contaminated regardless of soy sauce. The same menu sells 「二八蕎麦」 (20% wheat) beside 「十割蕎麦（数量限定）」 in one kitchen, plus 海老天/かき揚げ天/茄子天, 里芋の唐揚げ and 「き介の醤油唐揚げ」 (lunch) through a shared fryer. Rewrite the claim around the fu/chikuwabu/soba, and cite the menu page.

quote: Small, single-proprietress kitchen where every dish is made to order/by hand, which could in principle allow a dish to be discussed and adjusted if asked directly in Japanese — but this is not a documented policy, only an inference from the restaurant's small scale.
found: Shop page: 「お一人様でも歓迎 — 落ち着いたカウンター席で…おばんざいなので、少しずついろんな料理が楽しめます。女将の心温まる一品の数々は、どれも絶品。」, 席数 10, カウンター席あり. Tabelog reviews: 「女将さんがお一人で対応されている素敵なお店でした。カウンターのみのつくりですが…」 and 「カウンターの上に並べられた大皿料理が美味しそうでした！」
note: HALF TRUE, AND THE WRONG HALF IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. 'Small, single-proprietress kitchen' is confirmed (10 counter seats, 女将 working alone). But 'every dish is made to order' is contradicted by what obanzai IS and by both sources: the dishes are 大皿料理 already cooked and lined up along the counter. The record's own notes field says the same thing ('lines the counter daily with an ever-changing spread'). The claim's whole value to a celiac — that a dish could be adjusted on request — rests on a premise the evidence denies. Cut it or rewrite it as 'pre-cooked counter dishes; ask which contain 麩 or soy sauce'.

why: 'Limited vegan options' asserts that vegan options exist here. Nothing in any source documents a single one: the shop's only named dish is 車麩の煮物 (a simmered dish, i.e. dashi), the menu is image-only, Tabelog lists 料理（0）, and the record's own vegan_detail concedes 'nothing here can be assumed vegan without asking directly and in Japanese'. A label and a detail text that contradict each other is exactly the defect pattern; 'ask' is what the evidence actually supports.
